preview: An interview experience for Full Time roles (Risk Consulting and Tech Consultant) at PWC, consisting of an aptitude round, a technical round, a partner round, and an HR round.
content:
PWC Placement Experience

pwc came on campus on 17 August for Full Time hiring for the role of Risk Consulting and Tech Consultant. Whole process was based on your communication skills and resume.
Location: PAN India CTC: 9 LPA
Eligibility for a candidate was 6 CGPA and no backlogs.
They had 4 rounds of which all were virtual and proctered.
1. Aptitude Round (17 Aug)
Questions can be expected like CAT examination but easy.
Exam had 3 sections:
a. Verbal – To test your English, questions were fill in the banks, tenses, choosing wrong part of a statement and so on.
b. Numerical – Basic questions related to profit and loss, interest, probability and permutation and combination.
c. Logic – Pattern matching, finding next term in series.
This round didn’t need much preparation. Out of 250 students 110 were selected.
2. Technical Round (23 Aug)
All interview round was conducted in a single day on superset portal. Round lasted for 20 min. In this round different candidate were asked questions based on your resume. Your internship, projects and extracurricular activities. He asked me to explain any on project on the resume.
Although I wasn’t asked any technical questions, but basic questions on DSA, your core subjects (for me it was OS, DBMS and CN) can be expected. Indiabix is a good site to refer.
Whole round was to judge your personality and communication skills. You have to present yourself in front of them to keep the conversation keep going. They didn’t want much in depth explanation of your projects or internship. Everyone’s interview was friendly and chill. In this round your resume is very important, what you have stated in your resume must be true.
Out of 110 students around 70 were selected.
3. Partner Round
Before this round you would have been called for risk or tech consultant. I was selected for Risk Consultant. Here a partner can be referred as a senior at a management level who has been with pwc for a long time. For those who were selected for risk consultant, this round was tough.
Questions varied for candidate to candidate, main aim was to check how you perform under pressure. Situational questions were asked and some questions based on my resume. This round lasted around 20 min.
I was asked if I would become CEO of pwc what would be my immediate steps. How would I as a CEO work on to increase company’s revenue. What do you know about pwc? I told him I have a interest in finance, so he cross questions me with what have you been doing to learn. He questions me about any books I may have red and told to give a gist about it (I gave him a summary of rich dad poor dad). I also told him about that I was investing in stock for 2 years, he asked some questions related to my portfolio.
This round can be considered tough, there is noting that you can prepare for this round. You just need to keep the conversation going and think on your feet.
I don’t know exactly how many people were selected for next round, but to give a rough number it would be around 60.
4. HR Round
Almost everyone was selected who came in HR round. Round was quick lasted around 10 min.
Basic questions were asked about myself, what do you know about consultancy and pwc. Are you comfortable for reallocation and frequent travelling?
Every interview round must end with a question that you should ask to the interviewer. Apart from test, whole interview was based on communication skill, your resume and quick thinking.
You should really know about the company and the role that you were applying. Also, current news about company and pwc does. Basic HR questions like tell me about yourself, why consultant, why pwc and why should we hire you should be prepared for each round.
Whole interview process was concluded in 1-day result was announced around 10:30 in night.
Prepare from sites like interviewbit and geeks for geeks
https://www.interviewbit.com/pwc-interview-questions/
